focus: Playbook-side widening: 2,682-file citation census splitting gated links from unchecked inline citations; unresolved taxonomy with migrated-root fallback; canonical-case option check and live wrong-line anchor adjudication; expected-answer surface conformance

graphEvents.label: Live wrong-line anchor in canonical scenario

label: Live wrong-line anchor in canonical scenario

Playbook citation surface splits cleanly: 57 manual-testing-playbook trees hold 2,682 md files; 1,271 distinct .skilled/.opencode markdown links all resolve (links are already gated hard), while 706 distinct inline backticked citations (2,064 instances) are unchecked by any validator and carry the unresolved population (111 distinct raw, 102 still dead after argument stripping and the specs fallback). The unchecked surface is exactly the format the modes' own scenarios are written in.

The 102 dead inline citations decompose into five families: 30 placeholder/glob tokens ([###-short-name], <track>/<packet>/output, wildcards, ellipses), 30 .opencode/specs historical-provenance paths not resolvable even via the specs/* fallback (e.g. Source-phase lines citing pre-migration packets), 10 runtime/generated (.skilled/release/runs, .skilled/logs, .state), 10 migrated-named roots (.skilled/agents, changelog, commands, plugins), and 22 other including candidate move drift (.skilled/skills/cli-opencode/SKILL.md) that needs installed-layout-vs-repo-layout adjudication. Consequence: the playbook existence half needs the catalog-side expected-unresolved convention plus migrated-root fallback and trailing-argument stripping, and the domination by should-never-fail token families strengthens warn-only staging.

New live fixture: the canonical literal-naming scenario's failure triage cites create.sh line 1084 as carrying PROVIDE-DESCRIPTIVE-SLUG; the token actually occurs at lines 1060 and 1636, lines 1082-1088 carry session-scaffold print statements, and the file is now 2,289 lines. The wrong-line class is live on the playbook side, and it is invisible to both the catalog path:line anchor scan and the inline backticked-path scan because it is written as backticked-filename plus plain prose line number; corpus-wide the backtick-tolerant file.ext line N pattern finds exactly this 1 instance, and the first pattern returned 0 because of the backtick split.

The canonical option check false-positives on its own case: the scenario's 8 distinct flags include --trace-warnings, which is a Node runtime flag from the captured stderr hint, not a create.sh option; 7 of 8 resolve to declared create.sh options. A naive every-flag-must-exist-in-the-named-script check fails on the flagship fixture, reconfirming that command-grammar-aware attribution (which command each flag binds to) is the load-bearing cost of the option half.

Expected-answer surface is template-conformant corpus-wide: of 2,682 files, 1,382 carry SCENARIO CONTRACT, 1,261 Expected signals, 992 ### Expected, 952 ### Evidence, 668 ### Pass / Fail, and the structure appears outside sk-doc trees (sk-vision sample). But Expected is an excerpt, not a full output: the literal-naming Expected block shows 3 speckit warnings and exit 0 while Evidence adds Node ExperimentalWarning lines and Pass/Fail reconciles them. The lightest expected-answer check is assertion extraction over stated signals; the semantic question (is the expected value right) stays execution-bound.

Extractor lesson recorded as fixture material: the corpus-wide code-line scan first returned 0 because the one real instance writes the filename backticked and the line number outside the backticks; a backtick-tolerant pattern then finds exactly the stale anchor. Any new extractor for prose code-line refs must tolerate the backtick split.
